clue.text: Source of arcane ritual which, crushing all hearts, leads to complete anarchy

indicators.note: crushing the hearts squeezes them out of the word, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the word which spelt in full
H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts; 'all' means both H's in the word go

indicators.note: the leads of the next two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An occult rite that tramples every tender feeling and ends in total chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Both H's (hearts) go from WHICH, leaving WIC; the leads of 'complete anarchy' add CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicca is the modern witchcraft religion, the origin of many occult rites and ceremonies.

clue.text: Voluble person to meander and chatter when climbing

parts.note: to meander is to wind, as a path or river does

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: gab is idle chatter

explanation.surface: A talkative person rambling and gossiping on the way up a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A windbag is an informal term for someone who talks at tedious length.

clue.text: Fellow with name for feature of 1 Across

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a fellow or chap

explanation.surface: A man and his name presented as part of the witchcraft entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is a gathering of witches, a characteristic element of Wiccan practice.

clue.text: Adverse reaction from art venue moving opening much later

indicators.note: the opening letter of the venue word is shifted to a far later position in it

parts.note: a gallery is a place where art is shown

explanation.surface: Someone reacts badly because the gallery's opening night was pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: The G of GALLERY travels to the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is the body's hostile response to a substance such as pollen.

clue.text: One that'll fix print and film items?

parts.note: a paper is a printed newspaper
a clip is an extract from a film

explanation.surface: A device that repairs photographs and movie footage.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperclip is a bent wire that fastens sheets together.

clue.text: Criminal damage indication seen in fence

indicators.note: the damage word is placed within the fence word

parts.note: a picket fence is made of pointed stakes, so picket can mean fence
a pock is a pit or scar left on a surface, a mark of damage

explanation.surface: A sign of vandalism spotted on a fence points to a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' tempts as the criminal receiver of stolen goods, but here it is a wooden barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket is a thief who steals from people's pockets.

clue.text: Plot putting pressure on computer network

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
LAN stands for local area network

explanation.surface: A conspiracy to put strain on an office's computer system.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a scheme or design, the same as a plan.

clue.text: Crowd control running short at first in Surrey town

indicators.note: the shortened control word comes first, ahead of the crowd word
running short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as on a horse
the gate is the number of spectators at a match, so a crowd

explanation.surface: Stewards in a Surrey town struggle with crowd control early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowd control' looks like one phrase, but it splits: crowd is the gate (match attendance), control the rein. Reigate is a town in Surrey, south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Reigate is a market town in the English county of Surrey.

clue.text: Distributed information: rental property to be shielded by iron, then another metal

indicators.note: then means the next shield follows, the second metal wrapping around the result

parts.note: lead is a metal, Pb

indicators.note: the property word is protected inside the iron symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: A notice about a rental flat protected by iron and then a second metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Two layers of wrapping: iron is the inner shield and the second metal the outer one.
explanation.definitionFit: To leaflet is to hand out printed sheets, so leafleted means spread notices around.

clue.text: Artist getting line from bank

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who paints pictures
second meaning: a rope tying a boat to the bank or a mooring

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but this is a riverbank and the line is a boat's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides an artist, the word names a rope fixed to a boat's bow for mooring it.

clue.text: Coward possibly concealing start of violent story

indicators.note: the name holds the letter hidden within it

parts.note: Noel Coward was an English playwright; 'possibly' marks him as one example of a Noel

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of violent

explanation.surface: A timid person hides the opening of a violent tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' reads as a frightened person, but it is the playwright Noel Coward.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a long fictional prose story.

clue.text: Rich fools about to suppress a competitor mostly in racket

indicators.note: the shuffled letters press down on and enclose the rest
fooling about suggests messing with the order of the letters
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: Wealthy idiots muffle a rival in a noisy game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests a tennis bat, but it means a din: a charivari is a noisy mock serenade.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a cacophonous din of pans and kettles, so a racket or uproar.

clue.text: Side with little power in routine offering no new ideas?

parts.note: a bank is the side of a river

indicators.note: the power letter is placed inside the routine word

parts.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine
P is the short form of power

explanation.surface: Joining a faction with little clout in a tired routine that produces nothing fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bankrupt of ideas is to have none left, so creatively exhausted.

clue.text: Version later converted scoundrel

parts.note: V is an abbreviation for version, as in RV for Revised Version

indicators.note: converted means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A later edition turned a man into a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A varlet is an archaic word for a rogue or rascal.

clue.text: External contractor possibly more imaginative, ignoring Institute about piece of film

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes around the film piece
ignoring means leaving out the letter for Institute

parts.note: fancier means more elaborate or imaginative
a reel is a spool of film

explanation.surface: An outside contractor with more imagination skips the institute to work on a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the definition as an example: a freelancer is one kind of external contractor.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelancer is self-employed and hired by firms from outside, as an external contractor would be.

clue.text: Chap hugging stone with blasts of wind

indicators.note: hugging means the chap word wraps around the stone word

parts.note: a guy is a chap or man
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A man clutching a rock in a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusty weather has sudden strong rushes of air.

clue.text: Authorised edition went fast

parts.note: a document stamped is officially approved

explanation.surface: An approved printing sold out quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stampeded means rushed headlong, as a herd does in panic.

clue.text: Tradesman has complaint linked to register

parts.note: a carp is a petty grumble
to enter is to record or register

explanation.surface: A workman lodges a grievance with an official record.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a skilled woodworker, a classic trade.

clue.text: Impertinence and passion, grabbing cutie's latest piece of lingerie

parts.note: brass is British slang for cheek or nerve

indicators.note: grabbing means the passion word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion
the latest, or last, letter of the word cutie

explanation.surface: A cheeky and passionate grab at an attractive person's newest underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is a bra, a woman's undergarment.

clue.text: Increasingly tough tradesman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more butch, the comparative of butch

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as BUTCH + ER, a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch means rugged and tough, so its comparative works as more so; the noun is a meat trader.

clue.text: Wise person keeping feature of Glastonbury in preservation

indicators.note: keeping means the sage word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a sage is a wise person
Glastonbury Tor is a famous hill in Somerset, England; a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A wise elder conserving a Glastonbury landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury Tor is a hill topped by a ruined tower in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is the keeping of things to preserve them for later.

clue.text: Travel by bicycle exercises European Parliament after one's knocked out

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: knocked out means the letter for one is removed

parts.note: the Dail is the Irish parliament, a European one
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Cycling is good workout for MEPs once one of them has been floored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Parliament' looks like the EU body, but it means the Dail, Ireland's lower house; without I it gives DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to work a bicycle's foot levers, so to ride it.

clue.text: Demonstrate upturn in British rule with wise words

parts.note: to prove is to demonstrate

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn reads the letters from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Showing an economic recovery under British rule calls for wise words.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short traditional saying giving advice.

clue.text: The worst plan, denying Australian shelter

parts.note: the lees are the dregs, the worst part

indicators.note: denying means refusing entry to the letter for Australian

parts.note: an idea is a plan

explanation.surface: The most terrible scheme refuses an Australian any refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee side of something is the side sheltered from the wind.

clue.text: Leader seen in tent beside track

parts.note: the big top is a circus tent, so top stands for tent
to dog is to follow or track

explanation.surface: A chief spotted in a tent next to a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The top dog is the dominant person, the boss in a group.

clue.text: Shutter on window? Certainly German ratbag is keeping one hidden

parts.note: ja is German for yes, certainly

indicators.note: keeping means holding the letter for one inside
hidden confirms the letter is tucked away inside the other word

parts.note: louse and ratbag are both slang for a contemptible person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A window blind, yes in German, hiding something from a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalousie is a blind or shutter of angled slats for a window.

clue.text: Evil figure having cheers later for a more generous one

indicators.note: later means the thanks letters shift to further on in the word

parts.note: Satan is the Devil
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: The Devil getting a toast afterwards at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: TA leaves the middle of SATAN and goes to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is the kindly giver of gifts, a much kinder figure than the Devil.

clue.text: Fighter plane to take off? It's a failure

parts.note: F is the US designation for fighter aircraft, as in F-16
to lop is to cut off a branch

explanation.surface: A fighter jet trying to get airborne flops.
explanation.definitionFit: A flop is a total fiasco, something that fails.

clue.text: Arch duly constructed, with termination in Pompeii, carrying water

indicators.note: constructed means built anew, so the letters are put together in a new order
termination means the final letter of Pompeii

explanation.surface: A Roman arch built correctly at the end of a Pompeii aqueduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydraulic describes systems that convey water or liquid under pressure.

clue.text: One naked runner returning? Nothing exciting in this

indicators.note: returning means the letters come back in the opposite direction

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outside, so the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A streaker coming back across the field brings no excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: RUNNER without its ends gives UNNE; I + UNNE is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a state where nothing thrills.

clue.text: Ruddy shower doing for vegetable

parts.note: ruddy means red in colour
to pepper is to shower with shot or blows

explanation.surface: A blooming downpour ruining the vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' reads as the British mild swearword, but here it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A red pepper is a ripe capsicum, a vegetable used in cooking.

clue.text: Indifferent support restricting Liberal

indicators.note: restricting means confining the letter within the support word

parts.note: a base is a support

explanation.surface: An apathetic power base keeps Liberals in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasé means unimpressed through overfamiliarity, so unconcerned.
